_help: Your policy knobs. Every threshold needs a one-sentence 'why' (you'll be asked in the demo). evaluate.py warns while any 'why' still says TODO.
on_ezio_failure_why: If Ezio can't be reached we lose the tone and public-fact checks, so a person reviews the email; we fail closed but don't block a draft we never saw a problem in.
tier_decisions_why: GREEN sends; YELLOW and RED go to a manager, because a BLOCK needs a specific contradicted claim (from our data or Ezio's claims[]), and a low overall score alone doesn't prove the email is wrong.

tone.why: Normal friendly support emails score 90+, while several '!!!', all-caps words, or hype words drop tone below 60, which is the over-the-top style rule 4 sends to a manager.

bias.why: One loaded word like 'clearly' still scores 85; below 60 the email is pushing one side hard, which a customer-facing message shouldn't do.

agreement.why: A single polite 'good question' scores 75 and is fine; below 60 the email is piling on agreement with the customer, which is how agents end up confirming a customer's incorrect claim (rule 4).

when_accuracy_not_scored_why: Most support emails make no public-knowledge claims, and rule 5 says a missing accuracy score is not a reason to block; our own price-sheet and policy checks cover the company facts.
when_accuracy_unavailable_why: The fact-check service being down means a public claim (like a law) could be wrong without anyone seeing it, so a person reviews before sending.
